A Zod schema at the top level of a module is built as soon as the module is imported, even if you never validate anything with it. With hundreds of schemas, that makes every start slower.

The rule reports a chain of calls that starts with `z`, where `z` is imported or global, if it runs while the module loads. That includes static class fields and functions that are called where they're written. A schema inside another schema isn't reported again.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/zod-prefer-lazy-schema" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default. The ones that are commented out are unset by default.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/zod-prefer-lazy-schema" = ["error", {
  roots = ["z"],
  methods = [], # list of strings
  # factorySuffix = <string>,
  # lazyWrapper = <string>,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 1} */}
```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const User = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1),
  email: z.string().email(),
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { z } from "zod";

let user: z.ZodType | undefined;

export function userSchema() {
  return (user ??= z.object({
    name: z.string().min(1),
    email: z.string().email(),
  }));
}
```

`z.lazy()` doesn't build anything until it's used, so it's allowed:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { z } from "zod";

export const Comment = z.lazy(() => z.object({ text: z.string() }));
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roots` | `["z"]` | The names that a schema starts with, such as the `z` in `z.object()`. |
| `methods` | `[]` | Methods that build a schema, no matter what they're called on, such as `extend`. |
| `factorySuffix` | none | Also report calls to functions whose name ends in this string. |
| `lazyWrapper` | none | The name of your helper that builds a schema on first use. The message then shows how to call it. |

{/* bad {"options": [{"roots": ["v"]}]} */}
```ts
import * as v from "valibot";

export const Email = v.pipe(v.string(), v.email());
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"methods": ["extend"]}]} */}
```ts
import { User } from "./user";

export const Admin = User.extend({ level: 1 });
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"factorySuffix": "Schema"}]} */}
```ts
import { createUserSchema } from "./user";

export const User = createUserSchema();
```

`lazyWrapper` doesn't change what's reported. A schema in a function that you pass to a helper is allowed with or without it:

{/* good {"options": [{"lazyWrapper": "once"}]} */}
```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { once } from "./once";

export const user = once(() => z.object({ name: z.string() }));
```

## When not to use it

In a small program, or a server that starts once and runs for days, the time to build the schemas doesn't matter.
